key_insight: GroundCount augments vision-language models with explicit object-detection grounding so VLMs use concrete instance-level evidence (bounding boxes & counts) rather than relying solely on learned image-language priors, substantially reducing counting hallucinations while remaining lightweight and modular.
problem_solved: Persistent hallucinations and low accuracy in counting tasks by VLMs, where models guess or miscount objects despite strong visual inputs.
method: Run a fast CNN-based object detector (e.g., YOLO) to produce instance-level outputs: class labels, bounding boxes, and counts.
Convert detector outputs into a grounded input for the VLM (structured prompts, mask overlays, or region-conditioned tokens) so the VLM reasons over explicit spatial evidence.
Fuse detector-derived counts and regions with the VLM's reasoning step (post-hoc reconciliation or token-level conditioning) in a modular, low-overhead pipeline.
impact: Provides a practical, deployable way to reduce counting errors in multimodal systems, increasing trustworthiness and auditability of VLM outputs for real-world applications (e.g., robotics, inspection, and visual QA).

paper_title: GroundCount: Grounding Vision-Language Models with Object Detection for Mitigating Counting Hallucinations
paper_authors: Boyuan Chen, Minghao Shao, Siddharth Garg, Ramesh Karri, Muhammad Shafique
